name: Flood Response
summary: Riverine or flash flooding — evacuation, swiftwater rescue, road closures, and shelter coordination.

objectives: Establish the Incident Command Post (ICP) on high ground, well clear of the floodplain and any rising water.
Identify life-safety threats first; order evacuations for at-risk areas before the water reaches them.
Deploy swiftwater rescue teams to reported victims — no water entry except by trained teams in proper protective equipment.
Account for every person removed from a structure and track them to a designated shelter.
Monitor river and stream gauges and the weather; brief Command on the crest forecast each operational period.
Establish and publicize road closures — keep the public out of flooded roadways ("Turn Around, Don't Drown").
Coordinate with utilities to de-energize flooded areas and shut off gas where needed.
Log every rescue, evacuation, and searched-but-empty area with a time and location.
data.safety_message: Never drive or walk into moving water — 6 inches can knock you down and 12 inches can float a car. Water entry only by trained swiftwater teams in life jackets and helmets with throw bags. Assume all floodwater is contaminated and hides downed power lines, debris, and washed-out roadbeds. Buddy system at all times; everyone checks in and out with Base.
